comparison: Perfect agreement on oligodendrocyte-specific enrichment of ZDHHC9 and GOLGA7 (C3, C4, C32-C42). Both evaluations find the RNA-seq data across multiple datasets strongly supportive. Peer reviewers explicitly praised 'good data quality' and the comprehensive expression analysis.

Complete agreement on localization findings (C5-C7, C43-C51). Both evaluations accept the immunofluorescence data showing differential localization patterns. Peer reviewers noted the transgenic strategies 'strengthen the data and claims' without raising concerns about the localization evidence.

Full concordance on normal oligodendrocyte development findings (C8, C52-C58). Both evaluations find the comprehensive quantification across markers, timepoints, and CNS regions convincing. Peer reviewers accepted this without requesting additional validation.

Strong agreement on morphological abnormalities (C59-C65), though peer review also includes C9. Both evaluations accept the sparse labeling, 3D reconstruction, and Sholl analysis data. Peer reviewers acknowledged the study provides useful insights into XLID mechanisms without challenging the morphological findings.

Complete agreement on dysmyelination phenotype (C66-C73). Both evaluations find the electron microscopy and g-ratio analysis convincing. Peer reviewers accepted the distinction between dysmyelination and demyelination without critique.

Full concordance on cultured oligodendrocyte findings (C10, C74-C79). Both evaluations accept the shRNA knockdown data as supporting cell-autonomous effects. Peer reviewers implicitly endorsed this complementary in vitro approach through their statement about transgenic strategies strengthening claims.

Perfect agreement on MBP palmitoylation findings (C11-C12, C80-C84, C88-C89). Both evaluations find the ABE assay data from heterologous cells and brain tissue strongly supportive. Peer reviewers explicitly noted the study sheds light on palmitoylation mechanisms in myelination.

Complete agreement on selective effects on MAG (C85-C87, C90). Both evaluations accept these findings about other myelin proteins. Peer reviewers' general statement about 'good data quality' encompasses these biochemical analyses without specific concerns.

Partial agreement on mutant ZDHHC9 analysis (C91-C96). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED while acknowledging speculation about localization versus catalytic activity. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, noting 'a few claims might have needed better experimental support' that was partially addressed through revision. Both recognize the speculative nature of mechanistic interpretations.

Full concordance on background/clinical context claims (C1-C2, C13-C23). Both evaluations accept these citation-based claims about prior literature establishing clinical relevance. Peer reviewers affirmed the study's connection to XLID without questioning the background.

Divergent evaluations of speculative interpretations. OpenEval rates C112-C116 as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing these are speculative hypotheses requiring additional experiments. Peer review rates only C115-C116 as SUPPORTED, explicitly endorsing the authors' conclusions about oligodendrocyte contributions to intellectual disability. OpenEval is more conservative about mechanistic speculation.

OpenEval identified background knowledge claims (C24-C31, C37) as a distinct supported category representing established context from prior literature. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these background claims, likely incorporating them into their overall assessment of the study's foundation.

OpenEval identified methodological validation and contextual claims (C97-C111) as supported by prior literature. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these supporting methodological claims, though their acceptance of the overall experimental design implicitly endorses the methodological foundation.
